notes: Company: Saffron Pulse AI - builds an in-IDE AI pair programmer used by enterprise engineering teams.
Primary ask: deterministic, low-jitter streaming for single-line and multi-line completions; first-token latency critical.
TTFT target: ~40-80ms for local dev mode (single-token), 80-200ms acceptable for cloud-hosted suggestions depending on network.
Token budget model: want per-session and per-file token budgets; prefer server-side enforcement + client-side soft limits to avoid mid-completion truncation.
Backpressure: extension must handle when server batching increases latency — prefer graceful partial results + cancel/update signals rather than opaque timeouts.
Model/version pinning: workspace-level pinning needed (teams pin a stable 7B quantized variant). Automatic fallback path required for degraded nodes.
Quality vs cost: primary UX metric is time-to-first-token (TTFT) and jitter; willing to accept 5-10% higher token cost to hit TTFT SLA for paid tiers.
Implementation notes from SE call: try KV-cache warmup for repeated completions, prefetch top-k next-token logits for common snippets, reduce chunking size in streaming to lower TTFT jitter.
Security: enterprise customers require SSO + audit logs and optional KMS key for snippet encryption at rest. Legal asking about snippet retention TTLs.
Quote from CTO (paraphrase): 'If we can't make completions feel instant in the editor, adoption drops off quickly.'
Incumbent: using self-hosted endpoints + in-house batching; main pain: unpredictable tail latency and high token waste during retries.
POC metrics requested: 95th and 99th percentile TTFT; jitter (stdev TTFT); average token waste per completion; success rate for uninterrupted streaming sessions.
